scope: Measure USB Screen overhead separately within the ordinary M61/OPEN path and the linked VM PoC. Not a fresh main benchmark or a new matched cross-variant A/B/A.

method.scenario: Unchanged Turochamp, level 2, depth 8, book off, playing Black; first White move e2e3, 420 nodes.
method.clock: MCU micros(), accepted OK return -> entry into the next blocking APP key wait. Sample freezes at entry, before waiting for the user.
method.boundaries: Only two clock reads per blocking key call; no instrumentation in VM dispatch, and no profiler or terminal output during the timed interval.
method.statistics: Discard the first two searches; take the median of the two continuous samples and separately of the two headless samples. Never combine USB modes into one warm median.
method.headless: USB cable stays connected. USB Screen is detached before the game resumes from OK; the physical LCD remains active. The host observes 45 seconds without any screen frames, then reattaches only to verify the already-completed board.
method.completion_guard: MCU screen_begin=screen_end=0 for both detached runs in each cohort; a search not finished before reattachment would instead record screen_end=1 and fail.
method.board_guard: Complete eight-rank golden board required. Independently read the retained BASIC @(146)=420 through a separate owned probe after STOP, outside timing. Chess sources and algorithm are unchanged.

ordinary_M61_OPEN.headless_control: Detach normally, inject the same raw OK=37 through terminal kbd 25. Read the frozen MCU sample before validation reattachment.
ordinary_M61_OPEN.raw_harness_status: FAIL after this entire valid ordinary cohort; the subsequent linked cohort timed out on prof in its Black-selection menu, before any linked timed search. No failed linked timing is included here.
ordinary_M61_OPEN.raw_error: TimeoutError: prof received no response while linked VM owned the foreground

linked_VM_PoC.headless_control: Diagnostic-only PING arms detach after the next accepted key. Resident restores the physical LCD and releases virtual keys before starting the identical MCU timer and returning OK to the game. Read the frozen sample after board validation and STOP; no terminal call inside linked VM is required.

diagnostic_build.note: The second diagnostic firmware differs only in the extra headless-control hook; each reported USB-on/off comparison uses one identical firmware and APP set. Cross-variant differences are descriptive, not a replacement for the previous same-firmware VM A/B/A.

validation.timer_ASan_UBSan: PASS: accepted-key boundary, frozen next-wait capture, screen flags, micros wrap and one-shot diagnostic detach.
validation.disabled_timer_object: PASS: no key_wait_benchmark runtime symbols with the default flag 0.
validation.HIL_offline_tests: PASS: timer parsing, sequence/key/flag/duration rejection, separate USB cohorts, node probe, no-DFU/restore guards and complete-board oracle.
validation.resident_gates: PASS: Flash/RAM/stack budgets unchanged, all APP/stage/MSC/FS coexistence checks, native archive and USB CDC RX ELF gates.
validation.hardware: PASS: twelve completed searches with the identical full golden board, 420 nodes and e2e3; four valid headless intervals with screen_begin=screen_end=0 and no screen frames until validation. Every received USB packet/frame CRC checked.

conclusion: Without USB Screen, the ordinary Classic path is about 23.973 seconds and the linked VM PoC about 22.007 seconds. Screen overhead is about 4 percent here, not the entire three-second gap suggested by comparing unlike 25-second and 22-second runs. Do not claim a cross-platform winner: PicoCalc differs in CPU, runtime and screen mode. No cold-start or compilation speed claim from the discarded warmups.
